jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
jobs.description:
Supplier.io is the data foundation that enterprises build their supplier decisions on. Fragmented, duplicated, and unreliable supplier data quietly limits the ROI of source-to-pay platforms, analytics, risk, and AI initiatives, so we resolve, enrich, and continuously maintain the industry's most complete supplier identity, then put it to work for the teams that buy and the suppliers themselves. Relied on by companies across the Fortune 2000 for accurate data, our platform helps corporate procurement, finance, and compliance teams manage their vendor master, source diverse and sustainable suppliers, and mitigate risk, all from one verified identity instead of a dozen disconnected systems.

Our solutions turn that foundation into action: accurate data and continuous maintenance for teams managing a fragmented vendor master, sourcing intelligence built resolving even the hardest-to-identify suppliers, small, local, and diverse businesses, for teams tracking sustainability and compliance, and direct visibility for the suppliers themselves into where they stand with the enterprises that buy from them. Whether you're resolving vendor records, sourcing alternatives, or measuring program results, Supplier.io transforms complexity into clarity, so teams can lead with confidence and build supply chains that deliver for both business and community.

For more information, visit www.supplier.io.

The Opportunity

The Director, Data Architecture owns the strategy, standards, and team behind how data moves through Supplier.io, from source systems and web-scraping pipelines through ingestion, transformation, and governed delivery into the warehouses and marts the rest of the business relies on. You'll operate as a peer to our other engineering leaders, setting data architecture direction jointly with the CTO, while staying accountable for the reliability, quality, and governance of every data workflow we run.

You'll lead two distinct groups: a Data Engineering team building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and a Data Operations Engineering team running and maintaining the processes already in production. In the near term, before the team and its processes are fully built out, this role is hands-on: you'll be designing pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly, not just directing from a distance.

What You Will Do

Data Architecture & Platform Strategy

Own the multi-year data architecture strategy across our data warehouses and operational data stores, including evolving toward a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) lakehouse model.
Design and own our data lake and warehouse architecture, including the formation and population of data marts that serve analytics, product, and stakeholder reporting needs.
Set the orchestration strategy and standards for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT, and automated workflow management, and standardize the tooling used across the function.
Own the infrastructure and administration behind our data warehouses and pipelines, including capacity, reliability, and cost.
Own data governance end to end: the policies, standards, and practices for data quality, lineage, access, retention, and classification across every system of record.

Team & Execution Leadership

Build, lead, and grow two functions: Data Engineering, building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, running and maintaining existing production data processes.
Decide how the function is organized as it scales, including when and whether to add management layers beneath you to run day-to-day execution.
Stay hands-on early: design and review pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly until the team is built out to carry that execution independently, and stay close enough to the technology afterward to make credible architecture calls.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with engineering leadership to keep data architecture decisions aligned with company-wide standards.
Work closely with data engineering teams on technical planning and delivery for our core data products.
Partner with product, analytics, and other business stakeholders across the company to understand data needs and translate them into warehouse and data mart designs.

Data Quality & Compliance

Define and enforce data quality gates, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Own data access controls, classification, and retention policy across the data estate.
Ensure compliance-relevant and audit-sensitive data is handled according to governance standards as our data sources and customer base grow.

What You Will Need To Succeed

10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, including 5+ years in a Director or Manager-level leadership role owning architecture strategy and a team, not just individual delivery.
Deep, hands-on experience designing and operating cloud data warehouse or lakehouse architectures (Snowflake and/or BigQuery), including medallion (bronze, silver, gold) patterns.
Experience integrating a range of source systems (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and building ingestion and ETL pipelines from varied and unstructured sources, including web-scraping pipelines and background job orchestration.
A track record of building and scaling a data engineering or data platform organization, including deciding when and how to split engineering and operations functions.
Strong data governance background: establishing policies and standards for data quality, lineage, access, and retention in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment.
Experience setting technical direction jointly with peer engineering leaders and influencing architecture decisions across teams.
Excellent communication skills, comfortable setting strategy with peer leaders and reporting data platform health, cost, and risk directly to the CTO.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating or re-architecting data platforms following an acquisition or significant data source expansion.
Experience with orchestration tooling such as Airflow or dbt, and with scraping or crawling infrastructure at scale.
Background establishing data marts and self-service analytics layers for non-engineering stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability tooling (Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar).

As part of a leading provider of financial market infrastructure and post-trade services, you will work in an international environment where local expertise meets global perspectives. You will lead an experienced and close-knit team and ensure stable and secure IT operations with high availability requirements. Reporting to the Vice President, Marketing & Communications, the Director, Growth Marketing
owns Nicola Wealth’s demand-generation engine, translating marketing activity into measurable, qualified pipeline and revenue. This role is accountable for the full marketing digital funnel from paid and organic acquisition through conversion, nurturing and attribution and for building the data strategy, technology and reporting foundation that makes growth predictable, efficient and repeatable. Given the considered, relationship-driven nature of wealth management, the role places particular emphasis on educating and nurturing high-value, long-consideration prospects and on demonstrating a clear return on marketing investment.

Core Responsibilities:

Pipeline Ownership & Funnel Optimization — Own the end-to-end digital marketing funnel including paid media and advisor close rate journey. Evaluate and constantly optimize marketing’s contribution to qualified pipeline; define funnel stages, diagnose drop-off, and continuously improve conversion from anonymous visitor to marketing-qualified and sales-accepted lead.
Performance Analysis & Optimization — Use the multi-touch attribution and reporting provided by the Insights function to connect marketing spend and activity to pipeline and revenue, enabling confident, data-driven decisions on where to invest. Diagnose platform performance, set up in house media as needed for always on leads.
Website & Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) — Own the website as a conversion engine, leading a structured test-and-learn / A/B testing program to improve on-site conversion, performance and user experience.
Landing Pages, Lead Capture & User Experience — Design and optimize high-value landing pages and lead-capture frameworks — forms, offers and gated content — ensuring a seamless, trust-building experience aligned to each campaign and audience.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration — Lead, coach and develop the growth marketing function — team members, agencies and vendors — and partner across Sales, Content, Brand and Compliance to deliver integrated, measurable campaigns.
Customer Lifecycle Marketing (CLM) — Own lifecycle marketing across the full client relationship — onboarding, engagement, retention and deepening — extending marketing’s role beyond acquisition to nurture and grow existing client relationships.

Excellent communication, collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with a proven track record of partnering closely with Sales.

jobs.description:
About Northern Health Region

The Northern Regional Health Authority (NRHA) is responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering healthcare services across northern Manitoba, serving a population of more than 76,000 residents over an area that represents approximately 60% of Manitoba’s land mass. Through a network of hospitals, long-term care facilities, primary care clinics, and specialized treatment centres, the NRHA provides essential health services to diverse urban, rural, remote, and Indigenous communities throughout the region.

The region’s primary service hubs, Thompson, The Pas, and Flin Flon, offer the broadest range of healthcare services and provide critical support to communities across the North. The NRHA’s healthcare network includes six hospitals, four long-term care facilities, four primary care clinics, and two substance use and recovery treatment facilities, supported by dedicated healthcare professionals committed to improving health outcomes and advancing equitable access to care.

Northern Manitoba offers a unique blend of professional opportunity and exceptional quality of life. The region is renowned for its pristine lakes, expansive boreal forests, abundant wildlife, and year-round recreational opportunities. Residents enjoy access to outdoor activities such as fishing, boating, hiking, skiing, hunting, and snowmobiling, while benefiting from the strong sense of community and connection that defines life in the North.

The NRHA maintains regional offices in Thompson, The Pas, and Flin Flon, enabling close collaboration with communities, healthcare providers, Indigenous partners, and stakeholders across the region. Guided by a commitment to patient-centred care, health equity, and sustainable service delivery, the NRHA plays a vital role in supporting the health and well-being of northern Manitobans. The NRHA serves a population in which nearly three-quarters of residents self-identify as First Nations, Métis, or Inuit, underscoring the importance of culturally safe, equitable, and community-informed healthcare services throughout the region.

Download the Full Job Description: NRHA- Chief Executive Officer- Position Profile.pdf

Vision

Accessible, respectful, inclusive and safe healthcare for everyone.

Mission

We provide healthcare in a way that grows trust, inclusion and an understanding of patient needs to provide the best patient experience. We do that through people centered care and supporting our staff in a respectful, culturally safe environment. We are committed to meaningful partnerships with Indigenous partners, government agencies and other healthcare organizations as we strive to bring timely, equitable access to healthcare for the North.

Values

Trust, Respect, Integrity, Compassion, Humility

About The Chief Executive Officer

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) provides strategic, operational, financial, and cultural leadership for the Northern Health Region (NHR), ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality, sustainable healthcare services across northern, rural, and remote communities.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO is accountable for organizational performance, governance, workforce sustainability, system transformation, and effective partnerships with Indigenous communities, governments, staff, physicians, stakeholders, and health system partners.

A key responsibility of the role is advancing First Nations health equity, reconciliation, cultural safety, and anti-Indigenous racism initiatives through respectful partnerships, shared accountability, and community-informed decision-making. The CEO ensures culturally safe, trauma-informed, and distinctions-based approaches are embedded throughout organizational planning, service delivery, workforce development, quality improvement, and patient care.

The CEO serves as the Board's sole employee and is responsible for implementing Board direction, achieving strategic priorities, and ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, and governance requirements.

This position requires service and extensive travel to outlying communities within the region and the province.

Key Leadership Accountabilities

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Organizational Performance

Provide strategic leadership to advance the Northern Health Region's mission, vision, values, and long-term priorities while ensuring alignment with Board direction, provincial healthcare priorities, community health needs and Indigenous self-determination and shared leadership frameworks.

The CEO serves as the primary advisor to the Board and is accountable for organizational performance, governance excellence, and achievement of strategic objectives.

Lead the implementation, evaluation, and ongoing refinement of the Regional Health Plan and organizational priorities.
Monitor organizational performance and report progress, risks, opportunities, and outcomes to the Board.
Recommend strategic initiatives, policies, and long-term plans that support organizational sustainability and improved health outcomes.
Establish organizational priorities and strategic direction within Board-approved policies and governance frameworks.
Promote innovation, accountability, continuous improvement, and system-wide performance excellence.
Ensure organizational performance, legislative compliance, and achievement of Board expectations.
Indigenous Partnerships, Reconciliation & Health Equity

Advance meaningful partnerships with First Nations communities, leadership, and organizations while championing reconciliation, Indigenous health equity, cultural safety, anti-Indigenous racism initiatives and Indigenous self-determination through the integration of Indigenous governance principles across organizational leadership, strategy, and decision-making.

Foster respectful, collaborative relationships with First Nations leadership, communities, and organizations.
Advance reconciliation, Indigenous health equity, cultural safety, and anti-Indigenous racism initiatives across the organization.
Support the development and implementation of distinctions-based, community-led health and wellness priorities.
Establish shared accountability for Indigenous health outcomes through meaningful engagement, performance measurement, and transparent reporting.
Promote Indigenous workforce recruitment, retention, leadership development, and representation.
Champion the integration of Indigenous knowledge, cultural practices, and traditional healing approaches where appropriate.
Ensure meaningful engagement with Indigenous leaders, Elders, Knowledge Keepers, and community members in shaping organizational direction, strategic priorities, and healthcare service planning.
Ensure Indigenous health priorities are embedded within strategic, operational, and service planning activities.
Quality, Patient Safety & Service Excellence

Provide leadership to ensure the delivery of safe, high-quality, culturally responsive, patient- and family-centred care across all communities served by the Northern Health Region.

Ensure high-quality, accessible, and sustainable healthcare services are delivered throughout the Region.
Foster a culture of quality improvement, patient safety, risk management, organizational learning, and service excellence.
Monitor service quality, access, patient experience, and clinical and operational outcomes.
Ensure compliance with accreditation requirements, professional standards, legislation, and regulatory obligations.
Embed cultural safety, equity, and anti-racism principles within quality and patient safety systems.
Lead organizational participation in accreditation and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
Ensure organizational practices minimize risk and support effective management of patient and corporate liability.
Financial Stewardship, Risk Management & Operational Excellence

Ensure the effective stewardship of financial, human, physical, and technological resources to support sustainable healthcare delivery and long-term organizational success.

Oversee organizational budgeting, financial planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public resources and strong financial accountability.
Maintain effective governance, procurement, enterprise risk management, and internal control practices.
Make executive decisions regarding service delivery, resource allocation, workforce planning, and organizational performance.
Balance community needs, operational priorities, stakeholder interests, and fiscal responsibilities.
Support long-term organizational sustainability, operational effectiveness, and responsible growth.
Advance modernization, innovation, and evidence-informed decision-making across the organization.
Workforce Leadership, Culture & Talent Development

Cultivate a high-performing, inclusive, respectful, and culturally safe organizational culture while ensuring a sustainable workforce capable of meeting the healthcare needs of northern Manitoba.

Foster a culture grounded in respect, inclusion, cultural safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Provide leadership, coaching, mentorship, and support to the Executive Leadership Council and senior leaders.
Support leadership development pathways that strengthen Indigenous representation in senior leadership positions and across all levels of the workforce.
Promote Indigenous workforce recruitment, retention, leadership development, succession planning, and representation as a critical component of organizational excellence and culturally responsive healthcare delivery.
Establish and monitor performance expectations and support effective performance management processes.
Advance leadership development, succession planning, employee engagement, workforce wellbeing, and talent retention strategies.
Ensure compliance with applicable employment legislation, collective agreements, policies, and workplace practices.
Support effective onboarding, leadership integration, and development of future organizational leaders.
Ensure a workplace culture that is safe, respectful, and free from racism and discrimination.

About Northern Health Region

The Northern Regional Health Authority (NRHA) is responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering healthcare services across northern Manitoba, serving a population of more than 76,000 residents over an area that represents approximately 60% of Manitoba’s land mass. Through a network of hospitals, long-term care facilities, primary care clinics, and specialized treatment centres, the NRHA provides essential health services to diverse urban, rural, remote, and Indigenous communities throughout the region.

The region’s primary service hubs, Thompson, The Pas, and Flin Flon, offer the broadest range of healthcare services and provide critical support to communities across the North. The NRHA’s healthcare network includes six hospitals, four long-term care facilities, four primary care clinics, and two substance use and recovery treatment facilities, supported by dedicated healthcare professionals committed to improving health outcomes and advancing equitable access to care.

Northern Manitoba offers a unique blend of professional opportunity and exceptional quality of life. The region is renowned for its pristine lakes, expansive boreal forests, abundant wildlife, and year-round recreational opportunities. Residents enjoy access to outdoor activities such as fishing, boating, hiking, skiing, hunting, and snowmobiling, while benefiting from the strong sense of community and connection that defines life in the North.

The NRHA maintains regional offices in Thompson, The Pas, and Flin Flon, enabling close collaboration with communities, healthcare providers, Indigenous partners, and stakeholders across the region. Guided by a commitment to patient-centred care, health equity, and sustainable service delivery, the NRHA plays a vital role in supporting the health and well-being of northern Manitobans. The NRHA serves a population in which nearly three-quarters of residents self-identify as First Nations, Métis, or Inuit, underscoring the importance of culturally safe, equitable, and community-informed healthcare services throughout the region.
